top_signal.title: Built a $6–7k/month business but can't scale beyond myself. Should I keep trying or get a job and start over?
top_signal.summary: I'm 36, based in northern Europe, and have been running my own language education business for a few years. I'm at a crossroads and would appreciate advice from entrepreneurs who've faced something similar.    Some background:    I started teaching my mother tongue to expats and eventually turned it into a business. I've developed a structured curriculum, built a website, figured out paid advertising, established a sales process, and built a customer base.   During decent months, the business generates around $6–7k in revenue. I've also landed larger corporate contracts.   So there's clearly demand. But despite all this,  I'm still the business.  I handle marketing, sales, customer relationships, administration, and most of the teaching.   I'm increasingly questioning whether I've built a business or just created a demanding job for myself.    Problem 1: The business is interfering with my personal life.    Most customers are working professionals who want evening lessons. My girlfriend gets home around 6 PM, which is often exactly when I start teaching, sometimes until 10 PM.   We barely see each other on those evenings, and it's becoming a real problem.   I got into entrepreneurship partly for the freedom, but right now I have less control over my schedule than I would with a regular job. I don't want this to be my lifestyle for the next five years.    Problem 2: I've tried delegating, but customer retention suffered.    The obvious solution is hiring teachers and focusing
